display.title: Episode 30: The Forbidden Road, Chapter 1 (Yud-Beis Tammuz)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's summer kickoff: wealthy, short-tempered Reb Beryl fires his son's teacher in anger, then loses everything in one moment on a forbidden street. Plus a word on Yud-Beis Tammuz.
display.summary_long: At the start of summer 5742, Uncle Yossi promises that the program will continue all summer and reminds campers to keep their souls on vacation too, with davening, Torah and tzedakah every day. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, he teaches that learning Torah must lead to action and good midos, especially never losing one's temper. A boy with four names recites the Shema in Studio 604. The story, introduced as 'Rabbi Beryl Learns a Lesson', tells of a rich, learned but stingy and boastful man with a terrible temper. When his son's melamed teaches that wealth and poverty are in Hashem's hands and can change in a moment, Reb Beryl angrily throws him out. Walking off his anger, he is stopped by an officer for being on a street where Jews may not walk on Sundays and, confused, signs a paper that hands all his property to the government. Penniless in one moment, he heads to his Rebbe for advice; the answer comes next week. A listener's letter is read, and Uncle Yossi explains that this Shabbos is Yud-Beis Tammuz, the day the Frierdiker Rebbe was freed.
display.lesson: Learning Torah must lead to good deeds and good midos; never lose your temper, and remember that wealth is in Hashem's hands.

advisories.note: Jews are barred from certain streets on Sundays; an officer tricks a Jew into signing away all his property.
